content: Tracking changes to a specific page can only be done through the page history. The link to the page history is located at the top of the page, between the edit and move links. The history page contains a list of edits, which can vary in length. By default, it displays 50 edits per page, but this can be increased to 500. Each row in the history typically includes the following: (cur): This link shows the difference between the selected edit and the current version of the page. (last): This link shows the difference between the selected edit and the one immediately preceding it. Radio buttons: Two radio buttons are present per edit, one in each column. Selecting one button from each column and clicking Compare Selected Versions will display the differences between the chosen edits. Timestamp: The time the edit was made is displayed, such as 18:00, 15 April. The start of a new day is also marked in the history. Editor’s name: The username of the individual who made the edit is shown, e.g., Mia Kristos. Minor edit indicator: If an m appears, it signifies that the user marked the edit as minor. Edit summary: The user’s comment on their edit is displayed, or if no comment was provided, it may show a null description. Section title: If the user edited only a specific section of the page without changing the default edit summary, the section title will be marked. A small arrow will link directly to the edited section. The page history allows you to browse back to the page's creation or, in most cases, to the last history purge. Occasionally, Urban Dead wiki page histories are frozen to conserve database space. The Recent Changes link is located in the navigation menu on the left-hand side of any wiki page. It displays a list of the most recent changes made to any page in the wiki. The length of this list depends on the options selected at the top of the page. Each row in the list typically includes: (diff): This link shows the difference between the selected edit and the one immediately preceding it. (hist): This link takes you to the page's history. Quick glance indicators: N indicates that the page is new. m indicates that the user marked the edit as minor. A lack of patrolling means the edit has not been verified by another wiki user. Patrolling can be done from the diff screen, though this feature is rarely used in the Urban Dead wiki. Edited page link: The name of the page that was edited, with a link to it. Timestamp: The time the edit was made, such as 12:00. Editor’s name: The username of the individual who made the edit, e.g., Mia Kristos, along with a link to their talk page. Edit summary: The user’s comment on their edit, or a null description if no comment was provided. Section title: If the user edited only a specific section of the page without changing the default edit summary, the section title will be marked. A small arrow will link directly to the edited section. All edits made under a particular date will appear under that date's header. To view a user’s contributions, visit their User Page. A link titled User Contributions will appear in the lower left corner. Clicking this link will take you to a page titled Special:Contributions/Username, where Username is the name of the user whose contributions you are viewing. For example, clicking User Contributions while viewing Mia Kristos’s user page will take you to Special:Contributions/Mia_Kristos. If you are logged in, you can view your own contributions by clicking My Contributions in the upper right corner of the page. The User Contributions page is similar to Recent Changes, but it only displays edits made by the specific user. Each row typically includes: Timestamp: The time and date the edit was made, such as 12:00, 1 January 2006. A small arrow will link directly to the edited section. (top): This indicates that the listed edit is the most recent edit to that page. The Related Changes link is located in the toolbox on the left side of a wiki page. This feature is similar to Recent Changes, but it only lists changes to pages linked from the current page. For example, clicking Related Changes for a help page will show changes to all the help pages listed in the menu at the bottom of that page. Pages that cannot be edited, such as those in the Special namespace, will not be listed. At the top of each editable page, there is a tab labeled Watch (or Unwatch if the page is already on your watchlist). Clicking this tab will add or remove the page from your watchlist. You can also manage your watchlist by clicking Show and Edit complete watchlist on the watchlist page. When a page is on your watchlist, it will appear in bold in most change lists. The watchlist page itself is similar to Recent Changes, but it only lists changes to pages you are watching. This option is available in your User Preferences under the Email section. You will receive one email per page change and will not receive further notifications until you visit the page. Keep in mind that wikis are dynamic environments with frequent changes, so consider this when deciding whether to enable email notifications.
